cards.text: Friend, pull up a stool, because this one's heavy. Herod the tetrarch, a ruler in the land, hears the reports about Jesus. And Herod has a theory.

cards.question: Herod tells his servants who he thinks Jesus really is. Who does Herod say He is?

answers.text: John the Baptist risen from the dead

cards.question: Herod tells his servants that John rising from the dead is why miraculous powers are at work in Jesus.

cards.text: To rise from the dead, John would have to die first, so Matthew rewinds the tape. Herod had arrested John, the man who baptized Jesus (Matthew 3:13-16), bound him and put him in prison.

cards.question: Herod locked John up on account of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife. John had been telling Herod it is not ___ for him to have her.

cards.text: John keeps telling the ruler what he doesn't want to hear, and now he's in chains. Herod wants him dead, but he holds off.

cards.question: Herod wants John dead. What's holding him back?

answers.text: He's afraid of the chief priests

cards.text: The people regard John as a prophet, so Herod's like a manager who wants to fire the guy the whole office loves. Every time he heads for that desk, every head in the room pops up.
Then comes Herod's birthday, with guests all around. The daughter of Herodias dances before them.

cards.question: The dance by the daughter of Herodias leaves Herod unimpressed.
Herod is so pleased with the dance that he makes the girl a promise with an oath. What does he promise her?

cards.text: WHATEVER she asks, sworn with an oath. Friend, I once told a baker he could have whatever was on my cooling rack, and I watched four dozen cookies leave in one apron pocket. And that was just cookies.

cards.question: Before the girl tells Herod what she wants, her mother is the one who prompts her.
Prompted by her mother Herodias, what does the girl ask Herod for?

cards.text: The king is grieved. I bet you could hear a pin drop at that party.

cards.question: Herod is grieved by the girl's request, but because of his oaths and his ___, he orders that her wish be granted.

cards.text: So he sends to have John beheaded in the prison. John's head is brought in on a platter and presented to the girl, and she carries it to her mother.

cards.question: John is gone, but he isn't forgotten. Then John's ___ come and take his body and bury it.
After burying John, his disciples go and tell Herod.

findings.problem: "John keeps telling the ruler what he doesn't want to hear" states Herod's feeling as fact. Matthew 14:3-5 never says Herod didn't want to hear John, and Mark 6:20 says Herod listened to John gladly. Mark the guess as Papa Dorin's own, or drop the feeling and keep only what the text says.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: "with guests all around" uses the guests detail from Matthew 14:9, but the card cites only Matthew 14:6. Widening the citation to 14:6-9 would take in verses 7-8, which the card doesn't tell. Drop the guests detail instead, since "danced before them" already says others were there.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
